messages:
maya: heads up — customer AtlasPay on Dedicated is seeing repeated 503s and token-level throttling during a traffic spike. Seems autoscaler didn't add replicas fast enough. filing here before full support escalates.

samir: @maya timeline? when did spike start and what did metrics show?

maya: spike started ~10:14 PST, peak qps ~3x baseline for ~4 minutes. alerts fired for latency and 5xx at 10:17. customer repro steps: run burst load via our client for 30s -> 50% of requests 503.

carlos: any errors in the runtime logs? container OOM / crashloops?

maya: logs show request queueing + 429s from the rate limiter then 503 from gateway. no crashloop. example snippets below: 
```
[10:16:58] request_id=abcd error="no healthy backends"
[10:17:02] token=--- dropped: queue_len=120 scale_state=waiting_for_replicas
```

liz: can you paste kubectl HPA + deployment? suspects: HPA thresholds + minReplicas too low + model load cold-start time.

maya: pasted: 
```
$ kubectl get hpa inference-model -n dedicated-rt
NAME               REFERENCE              TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-model    Deployment/inference   85%/80%   1         10        1          12h

$ kubectl describe hpa inference-model -n dedicated-rt
... metrics: cpu average utilization 12% (target 80%)
```
HPA not firing because CPU metric low (we use request-based queue length metric upstream). scaling controller needs correct metric source.

samir: ah, we're using custom request queue metric (redwood/queue_length) but looks like the HPA is still wired to cpu. could explain scale-up lag for network-bound workloads.

maya: also saw pod startup time: image pull ~8s, container ready -> model load ~45-70s depending on model. so even if replica created, it won't serve instantly.

autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler event: insufficient nvidia-gpu nodes in pool 'dedicated-gpu-pool', scale-up 0->1 requested, pending quota. (10:18:15)

liz: that is important — platform was blocked by node quota. cluster couldn't add node fast enough, so pods stayed Pending/ContainerCreating. we need to check provider quota and burst capacity.

carlos: immediate mitigation suggestions? customer needs relief now.

samir: 1) temporarily increase minReplicas to 3 for that deployment (reduces cold starts). 2) enable a short-lived warm pool / keep-alive traffic to keep model cache warm. 3) if node quota is the blocker, request burst capacity or fallback to smaller model variant.

maya: applying quick patch to raise replicas now: 
```
kubectl scale deploy inference-model -n dedicated-rt --replicas=3
```
(note: will increase cost, but mitigates errors)

maya: after scale command, pods started pulling images but one stuck in ContainerCreating due to GPU driver init (seen before). ETA 2m for first new replica to serve.

liz: longer-term fixes: 
- switch HPA to use redwood/queue_length or custom metrics adapter so scale is request-driven not CPU-driven
- increase minReplicas for critical customers or add reserved pool (pre-warmed replicas)
- implement async request queuing + synthetic warmup call on scale-up to pre-load model weights
- add alert that correlates queue_length vs replica_count and node pool quota to detect blocked scale-ups

samir: +1. also add a runbook for support: steps to triage (check HPA wiring, check cluster-autoscaler events, check node pool quota, inspect pod events for ImagePullBackOff/GPU readiness, scale replicas or switch model variant).

carlos: noted, I have the customer on a short hold and will inform them of the temporary scaling increase. please keep this thread updated with timings. :thumbsup:

maya: will follow up with timeline + postmortem. next actions: update HPA metric to queue_length (PR created), request quota bump for gpu pool, and add warm-pool plan to roadmap.

autoscaler-bot: action recorded: scale decision executed by maya at 10:22 (scaled to 3). cluster event: node provisioning started at 10:23.

liz: good. once we confirm model loads on new pods and request failure rate drops, we can close the support ticket.

maya: 10:28 — first new pod Ready and serving, 503 rate dropped to 0. customer confirmed degraded->ok. will open a follow-up for root cause/changes. :white_check_mark:
